producer.nose: Sherry leads, with sweet caramel and butterscotch, then a corn-whiskey base.
producer.palate: Corn sweetness meets sherry notes of dried fruit, almond and bitter chocolate.
producer.summary: Blend of 4+ year straight bourbon, straight rye and light corn whiskey finished with 15-year oloroso sherry; positioned as a 'Kansas City Style' whiskey.

critics.nose: Subtle sweet berries reminiscent of a dessert wine, cranberry sauce, caramel and autumn spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, clove).
critics.palate: Soft honey-butter sweetness first, then growing heat and a charred crème brûlée caramel note.
critics.finish: Reviewer found it harsh and falling short of the nose's promise.
critics.summary: Above average for the price; best suited to classic cocktails.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of straight bourbon, straight rye and light corn whiskey, plus 15-year oloroso sherry

notes: Critic review is from 2016 and may reflect an earlier batch.

producer.nose: Caramelized orange and fresh bread, with orange blossom and cut grass.
producer.palate: Toasted cedar, five spice, sunflower seed and cinnamon; mid-palate of chocolate cherries and buttered popcorn with cherry-cola jam character.
producer.finish: Long and drier: sage, mint and a little toasted coconut.
producer.summary: Pot-distilled limited annual bottled-in-bond rye; 6 years on producer page.

critics.nose: Dry yet syrupy, with rye grain and grass, brandied dark cherry, sanded oak, baking spice and a faint creosote note.
critics.palate: Dark cherry and caramel with baked apricot, syrupy texture and creosote undertone.
critics.finish: Lingering dark cherry, creosote-caramel and syrupy chocolate with gentle heat.
critics.summary: Rated 'Yes' (worth buying); decadent, approachable and distinctive; 2022 release, 6 yr, 100 proof.

critics.nose: Baking spice, toasted oak, caramel, vanilla, honey, baking chocolate, dried fruit and maple.
critics.palate: Thick and spicy: clove, cinnamon, black pepper, then cocoa, honey, toasted oak and dried fruit.
critics.summary: 93 points; scale not stated on the page. 2021 inaugural release, nearly six years old, 50% ABV.

notes: Producer page gives 6 years (input says 4+). Release years vary (2021, 2022); mash bill from one source (a reviewer said 4% malted rye) so treat as approximate. Producer-page awards (SFWSC gold, 94 UCS) not recorded as critic entries.

producer.nose: 2023 edition: buttered popcorn, French toast, maple, smoky cedar, woody tobacco, black pepper, caramelized orange, hint of tropical fruit.
producer.summary: Limited solera-style blend of Kansas City whiskey, bourbon, rye and corn whiskey with oloroso sherry; 2026 edition described as bigger and bolder than 2025.

critics.nose: Cherries jubilee, baked pie crust cinnamon, warm oak, green apple, ripe peach and dark fruit compote.
critics.palate: Light cigar smoke, bright red wine notes, dark molasses, cigar box and baking chocolate.
critics.finish: Oily texture, lasting dark cherry and plum with a trace of white sugar.

critics.nose: Sweet caramel snickerdoodle, marshmallow, maple and graham cracker, shifting to buttered popcorn and some sulfur/shoe polish.
critics.palate: Sherry-led: toasted pecan, oxidized apple, yellow peach, toasted coconut, golden raisin, lemon zest.
critics.finish: Long: yellow plum, graham cracker, pencil shavings, campfire smoke.
critics.summary: 2023 release; page shows a 5/5 style rating but scale unclear, so not recorded as score; reviewer ambivalent on the flavor combination.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of Kansas City whiskey, straight bourbon, straight rye, light corn whiskey
facts.cask: Solera of old casks plus 15-year oloroso sherry

notes: Release-specific bottling: producer notes are for 2023 edition, critic scores for 2025 (8/10) and 2023 (unscored). Different years taste different.

Only Still 630 pages found were Due Process Cask Strength single barrel (130.6 proof, over 5 yrs) and a Small Batch Missouri bourbon (90 proof); neither matches the 92-proof Due Process listing, so nothing recorded. No critic reviews found. Further searching blocked by search budget.

producer.nose: Lime and lemon, leaf, white nectarine, white flowers and bosc pear.
producer.palate: Key lime, nectarine, honeysuckle and kumquat; light-to-medium body with bright, balanced acidity.

critics.palate: Juicy apple, peach and ripe melon with lemon, pomelo and a touch of fresh ginger.

critics.nose: Lifted white grapefruit zest and piney fresh herbs.
critics.palate: Floats lightly with a delicate floral touch and fresh acidity.
Pear, melon and citrus with dried herb and wildflower hints.

notes: 2023 vintage, all via a single retailer page (wine.com). Page ABV 12.8 differs from input 13.5. Wine Enthusiast 2024 page was rate-limited and not read.

producer.palate: Crisp acidity with soft rich mouthfeel; ripe pineapple, crisp pear.
producer.summary: 2021 vintage; page lists a blend of Albariño, Malvasia Bianca and Chardonnay.

notes: Only retailer-reproduced producer copy (2021 vintage, The Prisoner Wine Co. Unshackled). Page ABV 14 differs from input 13 and the blend listed is not pure Sauvignon Blanc; verify label/vintage. Wine Enthusiast and Wine Spectator pages (2020) not read: rate-limited or paywalled.

producer.nose: Restrained and less tropical than earlier vintages, opening to citrus, lime leaf and apricot.
producer.palate: Intense with passionfruit, citrus and a saline note.

critics.palate: Fine texture, bright citrus, fresh herbs, a touch of tomato stalk.
critics.summary: Fragrant, juicy wine from a very dry vintage.

critics.palate: Energetic and clear, with guava, citrus tang and blackcurrant leaf.
critics.summary: Still a luminous star of the style.

critics.nose: Green apple and a salsa-verde herbal note.
critics.palate: Punchy, crunchy and high acid with chalky mid-palate texture.

notes: 2024 vintage. ABV 13.5 per Decanter and wine.com (input says 13). Wine Spectator page for 2024 is paywalled (score not visible).

producer.nose: Citrus, stone fruit and exotic florals.
producer.palate: Grapefruit, white nectarine, lemon curd and beeswax; tightly focused with barrel-fermented texture.
producer.finish: Nectarine, glace fruit and light smoky oak, with jasmine, honeysuckle and pollen.

critics.summary: Good balance and has aged well in bottle.

critics.palate: Coconut, toasted anise seed, sesame oil, Meyer lemon, sugared grapefruit; creamy body.
critics.summary: Graded A- (about 9/10 per the page); 2021 vintage, $65.

notes: Producer notes and Decanter/Wine Advocate scores are for the 2015 vintage (ABV 14 then; input says 13); Drinkhacker is 2021. Cloudy Bay's own site page was not found.
